business_problem: Nelen & Schuurmans wanted to make its Rana water-intelligence platform easier to use by turning complex documentation and workflows into guided assistance for hydrodynamics modeling users.
solution_summary: Nelen & Schuurmans worked with IBM Ecosystem Engineering to add a generative AI assistant to Rana, its hydrodynamics and water-intelligence platform. The solution uses IBM watsonx.ai together with IBM watsonx.data in a retrieval-augmented architecture that transforms documentation into indexed, semantically searchable knowledge and generates code snippets and guidance for users. IBM and Nelen & Schuurmans refined the source material with semantic chunking so the assistant could provide more grounded answers during modeling workflows. Users can ask questions through the application interface and receive relevant instructions, API-call guidance and contextual explanations without navigating manuals manually. The design improves accessibility for less experienced users while also creating a revenue path for premium prompt packs and advanced interactions, making the assistant both a usability feature and a commercial extension of the Rana platform.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.ai
solution_components.role: Generates guidance, answers and code snippets for Rana users during modeling workflows.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.data
solution_components.role: Stores and indexes refined documentation to support semantic retrieval and grounded responses.

data_flow: Rana documentation is semantically chunked and indexed in watsonx.data, retrieved based on user questions and then combined with watsonx.ai generation to return guidance, API snippets and workflow explanations inside the Rana interface.
business_outcome: Nelen & Schuurmans improved product usability, expanded the number of supported user interactions and opened a strong ROI path for premium generative features on Rana.
